This episode differs from the late 1990s ABA crisis in that the current Department operates under heightened scrutiny regarding ideological uniformity, diversity mandates, and institutional capture, shifting the friction point from mere market dominance and antitrust compliance to fundamental legal and policy disagreements over law school standards. It differs from the ACICS demise because ACICS was dismantled over lax academic outcomes and fraudulent practices under an administration explicitly hostile to lax oversight, whereas a revocation of the ABA would target a powerful, deeply entrenched legal guild over political and structural compliance disputes. The current episode is uniquely characterized by a convergence of bipartisan and ideological attacks on legal education monopolies, making the Department's willingness to exercise the ultimate penalty significantly more viable than in past decades.
